# IRIS MCP skills pack

Agent skills and the always-on rule for working with the IRIS MCP Server Suite. A skill that names the suite's tools shows its tool preset: the first of `core`, `developer` and `full` (the values of `IRIS_TOOLS_PRESET`) under which every tool it names is visible. `full`, the default, shows every tool.

## Knowledge skills

An agent loads a knowledge skill when its task matches the skill's description.

- `iris-mcp-interoperability`: Writing IRIS interoperability (Ensemble) components in ObjectScript: business service, process and operation classes and their method signatures, Ens.Request and Ens.Response messages, adapters, settings and message maps, synchronous and asynchronous sends, and why the production class XData, not the configuration tables, defines a production. Use when creating or editing a business host, a message class or a production class, or when a host does not compile, a request is not handled, a setting does not appear, or a configuration change does not last.
- `iris-mcp-objectscript-error-handling`: How %Status values and exceptions work in ObjectScript: making, testing, combining and reading a status, the Try and Catch method shape, ThrowOnError, ThrowStatus and AsStatus, what a runtime error looks like inside a Catch, and reading error text without its translated ERROR #N prefix. Use when writing a method that returns %Status, handling, rethrowing or logging an error, converting between exceptions and statuses, or putting error text that IRIS returned into a new error.
- `iris-mcp-objectscript-gotchas`: ObjectScript language traps that compile or run differently from what the code suggests: which macros a class gets without an Include, extra arguments, JSON null against a missing key in a dynamic object, object references inside $List, numeric-looking subscripts, New $NAMESPACE and Catch blocks, missing Ens classes, and Open timeouts. Use when writing, reviewing or debugging ObjectScript, or when IRIS reports MPP5610, PARAMETER, INVALID CLASS, INVALID OREF or CLASS DOES NOT EXIST and the cause is not obvious.
- `iris-mcp-objectscript-sql`: Running SQL from ObjectScript with embedded SQL and %SQL.Statement: the SQL table name of a class, SQLCODE 0, 100 and negative values, what INTO variables hold when no row is found, errors that appear only when a statement runs or a row is fetched, NULL against the empty string, and what %OpenId and %DeleteId return for a missing ID. Use when writing or reviewing &sql or %SQL.Statement code, or when a query reports SQLCODE -30 or -29, finds no row you expected, or returns an empty value.
- `iris-mcp-objectscript-unit-tests`: Writing and running %UnitTest tests in ObjectScript: the TestCase class shape and its setup and teardown hooks, which methods run and in what order, the common Assert macros and what they return, skipping a test, what happens when setup or a test fails, and running a class with %UnitTest.Manager and checking its totals. Use when creating or editing a %UnitTest.TestCase class, running IRIS unit tests, or when a run reports fewer tests than expected, zero tests, or a failure you cannot explain.
- `iris-mcp-system-classes`: Using the IRIS system classes from ObjectScript: what the Config, SYS and Security classes hold and when one answer needs two of them, class queries with fewer columns than the class, deprecated properties that still read but no longer follow the configuration, switching to %SYS and back safely, and counters of one process against the whole instance. Use when code calls Config, SYS or Security classes, switches $NAMESPACE to %SYS, reports system metrics, or fails with CLASS DOES NOT EXIST or NAMESPACE around a namespace switch.

## Workflow skills

Each is generated from the MCP prompt of the same name and walks an agent through one task with the suite's tools.

- `audit-security-posture` (tool preset `full`): A read-only audit of an IRIS instance's security: users whose password settings look stale or that may use a well-known default credential, every user and role that holds %All, services that are enabled without authentication or not needed, SSL/TLS configurations with a minimum TLS version below 1.2 or missing certificate paths, and whether auditing is on, ending in a report of recommended fixes; it changes nothing. Use when the user asks to audit, review or harden IRIS security, asks who holds %All, or asks whether services, SSL/TLS or auditing are set up safely.
- `check-system-health` (tool preset `full`): Runs one composite health check of an IRIS instance across its nine areas (journal, databases, license, locks, alerts, mirror, ECP, interoperability and the system) and follows each warning, critical or error finding to the tool that explains or fixes it, never running a destructive fix without the user's confirmation. Use when the user asks whether IRIS is healthy or wants a health or status check, or reports trouble with journal space, database size, the license, locks or alerts.
- `deploy-and-test-class` (tool preset `developer`): Deploys an ObjectScript class or package from local source files to IRIS with a glob-path load and compile, fixes compile errors in the source and loads it again, runs its unit tests, compares the returned total with the number of test methods because an early partial result looks like a green run, re-attaches to a run that is still going instead of starting a second one, and measures line coverage when the user asks for it. Use when the user wants to deploy, load or import ObjectScript source into IRIS, compile it, run its %UnitTest tests, or see their coverage.
- `diagnose-slow-query` (tool preset `developer`): Diagnoses a slow IRIS SQL query from its query plan, the maps and indexes the plan reads, and the statement's cumulative run-time statistics, looking for full table scans, missing indexes, hot statements and plan inefficiencies, then recommends a fix such as a new index or a rewritten WHERE clause without applying it. Use when the user says a SQL query is slow, asks why a query does not use an index, or wants a query plan explained.
- `edit-and-test-class` (tool preset `core`): Changes a few lines of an ObjectScript class directly in IRIS: reads the lines around the change, applies a guarded line edit that stores nothing when the class no longer matches what was read, compiles the class and fixes errors the same way, runs its unit tests and checks the returned total, and reports the diff. Use when the user wants a small fix or change to a class that lives in IRIS, especially one with no local source file, or asks to patch, compile and test a class in place.
- `find-patient-messages` (tool preset `core`): Finds a patient's interoperability messages by an identifier such as a medical record number, through a Search Table and in search windows of at most 7 days, lists the matching message headers, and reads message bodies only when the user wants the content, under the PHI data policy, which by default redacts or withholds them. Use when the user asks for the messages, HL7 traffic or message history of a patient or medical record number in an IRIS interoperability production.
- `promote-environment-change` (tool preset `developer`): Promotes configuration and code drift from one IRIS environment to another in review-before-write order, diff -> plan -> confirmed execute -> second diff: it compares mappings, System Default Settings, web applications, supported CPF settings and, given a spec, ObjectScript source, executes only the plan steps the user picks and confirms, and checks that the promoted drift is gone. It never removes an item that exists only on the target. Use when the user wants to compare two IRIS servers or environments, or to promote, sync or copy changes from one to another, such as from development to test.
- `provision-project-environment` (tool preset `core`): Provisions a new IRIS project environment in order: a DATA and a CODE database, a namespace over them, a user whose default namespace it is, and a web application, checking each step before the next, rolling back the completed steps when one fails, and naming the manual follow-up a new web application needs. Use when the user wants to set up or create a new IRIS project, namespace or application environment.
- `recover-stuck-production` (tool preset `core`): Diagnoses and recovers a troubled or wedged interoperability production along an escalation ladder, in order: status, queues and error logs first, then the recover action, and the clean action only when recover does not fix it, never wiping persistent business state unless the user explicitly accepts the data loss. Use when an IRIS interoperability production is stuck, troubled or suspended, messages are not processing or queues are backing up, or the user asks to restart or recover a production.
- `resend-failed-messages` (tool preset `core`): Resends failed interoperability messages for one configuration item, dry run first: it previews the match count and a sample, resends only after the user approves with an explicit confirmation, and then checks the new message headers. It states that a resend delivers the data downstream again and that the resend actions are writes disabled by default. Use when the user wants to retry, replay or resend failed or errored messages in an IRIS interoperability production.
- `run-external-backup` (tool preset `full`): Freezes an IRIS instance for an external backup snapshot taken at the OS or SAN level, waits while the user takes the snapshot, and always thaws the instance afterwards, even when the snapshot fails, then confirms that journaling resumed and checks the run in the backup history. Use when the user wants to back up IRIS with an external OS-level or SAN snapshot, or asks to freeze and thaw IRIS database writes for a backup.
- `trace-message-flow` (tool preset `core`): Traces one interoperability message flow from a session or message header ID: lists every hop, searches the session's message headers, reads the bodies that matter under the PHI data policy, draws a sequence diagram, and pulls the error log entries of each failing item, then reports where the flow failed and recommends next steps, never running a recovery without the user's confirmation. Use when the user asks what happened to a message or session, why a message failed or never arrived, or how a message moved through an IRIS interoperability production.

## Always-on rules

- `iris-mcp-objectscript-pre-write`: ObjectScript pre-write checklist. Its Claude Code form, `rules/claude-code/iris-mcp-objectscript-pre-write.md`, has no `paths:` scope, so it loads in every session of a project that installs it. `rules/agents-md/iris-mcp-objectscript-pre-write.md` holds the same text for `AGENTS.md`, between two marker lines.

## Layout

- `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`: one directory per skill, in the standard plugin layout.
- `rules/claude-code/<name>.md`: the always-on rule as a Claude Code rule file.
- `rules/agents-md/<name>.md`: the same rule as an `AGENTS.md` section, between the lines `<!-- IRIS-MCP-RULE:<name>:BEGIN -->` and `<!-- IRIS-MCP-RULE:<name>:END -->`.
- `IRIS-MCP-THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md`: third-party notices and licence texts for adapted content.

## Third-party content

Content adapted from another project carries a header line as its first non-blank line after any frontmatter, and a row in the provenance table of `IRIS-MCP-THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md`. Read that file before redistributing the pack.
